sent:
Amrita —

Thanks for the straight ask. Here’s the teardown plus a 2‑week test you can run now.

Angle on “mud‑wins”
- Lead with motion if you can: a tight 3–5s clip of muddy knees vs. reinforced stitching, or water beading on Splash Raincoat.
- If video isn’t ready, use a macro static (stitching/knee panels) with a blunt line: “Reinforced knees. Free UK returns.”
- Run both: one video variant, one macro static, one carousel close‑up; let the account tell you.

What’s strong (use more)
- Reinforced knees and seams; GOTS organic; 30‑day free returns.
- The Leeds Lookbook shots feel real and colourful—great ad and hero fodder.

What to change this week
- Lead with a proof‑first hero and put one reassurance (returns/delivery) in the first screen.
- Add a simple fit cue on product cards (e.g., “true to size”) and a quick height/cm hint alongside ages.
- Pull Lookbook frames into the first screen of key pages, not just the Lookbook.

Three promise pages (one ad, one promise, one page)
1) Rain (Splash Raincoat + rainwear)
- Hero: water beading test; headline “Dry kids = longer play.”
- Proof bullets: construction detail; one parent quote.
- CTA: “Get the Splash Raincoat.”

2) Rough‑and‑Tumble (playproof bottoms)
- Hero: knees in action; “Reinforced knees. Playground ready.”
- Size/height microcopy; one durability line.
- CTA: “Shop playproof bottoms.”

3) Party (bright sets/dresses)
- Hero: twirl/colour pop; “Party‑bright, play‑ready.”
- Care note; simple fit cue.
- CTA: “Party‑ready outfits.”

Three ad concepts (ship each in 3 variants)
A) Mud Wins — video, macro static, carousel of post‑play close‑ups.
B) Rain Test — hose/squirt‑gun clip; shake‑dry moment; product under running water.
C) Hand‑Me‑Down — sibling handoff; year‑1/2/3 stack; short parent quote on longevity + planet‑kind.

How to measure
- Route each ad only to its matching promise page; keep a small homepage holdout for benchmark.
- Count cost per first order from each page and retire any creative after three weeks of falling click‑through; keep anything still climbing.

Evidence we can stand behind
- We don’t have kidswear‑specific CPA lifts to cite yet.
- Closest quantified result: for Oatside Kitchen (DTC food), moving ads from homepage to offer‑specific pages cut cost per first order by 38%. Same principle here: one ad, one promise, one page.

If helpful, I can send quick wireframe templates for the three pages.
